task.description: Run WF-02 Step 3's scope test first, then produce test specs and test code for REQ-027. Expected YES (two real Ecto.Schema modules with validating changesets, two migrations with a load-bearing conditional guard, three partial/unique index shapes and an FK referential action). Five carry-forward instructions accumulated from Steps 1b, 2c and 2d are in the dispatch prompt and must not be dropped -- two of them convert this requirement's SILENT-correctness invariants into exit-code gates, which is the highest-value work in this step.
acceptance_criteria: the WF-02 Step 3 scope test is run first and its verdict stated with reasoning
every one of REQ-027's 5 acceptance criteria has at least one runnable test that would fail if the criterion were violated
test specs are written under test/specs/ alongside the test code
no test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness; fixtures use per-test unique data; tests are self-sufficient
the FK referential action and the partial-index predicate are asserted from the live catalog, not from migration source
every tenant schema created by a test is dropped, including on the failure path

result.summary: SCOPE TEST (WF-02 Step 3, run first, re-derived not inherited) -- VERDICT: YES, in scope; the full TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR / TEST-RUNNER chain applies. Reasoning: Step 2a/2b's artifacts_out contain two real Ecto.Schema modules (lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex, instance_definition_snapshot.ex) whose changesets cast, validate lengths and declare named unique/foreign-key constraints -- executable logic whose return value changes if the cast list or a constraint name is wrong; two migrations that are .exs but emphatically NOT build config, since each change/0 executes real DDL against a real database behind a load-bearing `if prefix() do` conditional whose two branches behave differently (REQ-022 section 4's guard pattern); three independently falsifiable index shapes (a total unique index, a partial UNIQUE index with a predicate, a partial non-unique index with a different predicate); one foreign key with a specific referential action; and a 2-line change to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's tenant_scoped_migrations/0 manifest that changes what replay_migrations/2 does at runtime. 'Does this DDL actually produce the shape claimed' is a question only a real database can answer -- the opposite of REQ-013's mix.exs-alias case the scope test exists to divert. || WHAT WAS WRITTEN: test/specs/REQ-027.md (20 numbered test cases, each with the reason it exists rather than a restatement of the criterion), test/letflow/definitions/schemas_test.exs (pure, async: true -- reads only compiled module metadata via __schema__/1, __info__/1, Ecto.Enum reflection and Code.fetch_docs/1; zero Repo calls and zero :telemetry.attach, deliberately not repeating the ISS-0011 mistake) and test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs (real Postgres via Letflow.DataCase, async: false, sandbox switched to :auto because Ecto.Migrator needs a second independent connection; on_exit registered BEFORE the replay so every tenant schema is dropped on the failure path too). Both files match the shape of test/letflow/event_store/schemas_test.exs and migrations_test.exs rather than inventing a parallel style. || CRITERION -> TEST MAPPING (all 5 covered by runnable tests that would fail if violated; no @tag :skip, no TODO): AC1 'both migrations schema-per-tenant via :prefix, applying cleanly' -> migrations_test 'replay_migrations/2 applies both REQ-027 migrations and both definition tables land in the tenant's own schema, never in public' (the refute-in-public half is what proves :prefix is doing the work), 'tenant_scoped_migrations/0 registers both REQ-027 definition migrations' (REQ-022 section 4's other mandatory half -- a guarded-but-unregistered migration is inert forever and no other test here would notice), 'each definition table's real column set ... matches its Ecto.Schema module's field list exactly' (equality, not subset), plus schemas_test 'neither definition schema module pins a compile-time @schema_prefix (INV-DEF-7)'. AC2 'unique index on (name, version) and partial unique index on name WHERE status = active' -> migrations_test 'uq_definition_version is a total UNIQUE index over exactly (name, version)' (read from pg_indexes, not information_schema.table_constraints, which does not list Ecto's CREATE UNIQUE INDEX at all and would pass vacuously; asserts no WHERE clause, since a partial variant would enforce a strictly weaker rule under the same name), 'a second definition with the same (name, version) is rejected by uq_definition_version', 'uq_active_definition is a PARTIAL unique index over (name) whose predicate matches the literal Ecto.Enum actually dumps for :active', 'a second definition activated under a name that already has an active definition is rejected by uq_active_definition (PD-03)', plus schemas_test 'create_changeset/2 and update_changeset/2 both declare uq_definition_version and uq_active_definition by index name'. AC3 'nullable stage column and partial index on stage WHERE stage IS NOT NULL' -> migrations_test 'stage is a nullable column and an omitted stage lands as SQL NULL, which is what idx_def_stage's predicate depends on' (is_nullable = YES from the catalog AND a real round trip, because a stage landing as '' instead of NULL would make the predicate index every row and silently falsify PD-07's compactness rationale), 'idx_def_stage is a non-unique PARTIAL index over (stage) predicated on stage IS NOT NULL' (the non-unique half asserted explicitly: a unique index there would forbid two definitions sharing a stage label, which PD-07's open-ended labels permit), plus schemas_test 'stage is castable, optional on both changesets, and validated only for length -- no enum, per PD-07' (fed through the real changeset, so a validate_inclusion added later fails). AC4 'definition_id references process_definitions.id with no ON DELETE CASCADE, moduledoc states this is deliberate per PD-08' -> migrations_test 'the snapshot FK's referential action in the live catalog is NO ACTION (a), not CASCADE (c)' (also pins constraint name, referencing column, referenced table in the tenant's own schema, and referenced column, so 'confdeltype is a' cannot be satisfied by an FK onto the wrong table), 'deleting a definition that has a snapshot row is rejected, and the snapshot survives with its captured graph (PD-08)', 'a snapshot referencing a nonexistent definition is rejected as {:error, changeset}, not a raised error', plus schemas_test 'InstanceDefinitionSnapshot's moduledoc states the missing ON DELETE CASCADE is deliberate per PD-08' and 'InstanceDefinitionSnapshot's own public API is exactly create_changeset/2' with ProcessDefinition's two-function API as the negative control that proves the assertion discriminates. AC5 'both moduledocs cite src/design/definition.md (PD-01/PD-07/PD-08) as the ported source' -> schemas_test 'both definition schema modules' moduledocs cite R-Co's src/design/definition.md and its PD-01, PD-07 and PD-08 sections' and 'both moduledocs carry REQ-027's mandated schema only scope note' -- both read the compiled Docs chunk via Code.fetch_docs/1, never the .ex file as a string, and pattern-match the 'documented' shape so a deleted (:none) or hidden (:hidden) moduledoc raises rather than passing vacuously. || FIVE CARRY-FORWARDS, ALL HANDLED. (a) BOTH SILENT-CORRECTNESS INVARIANTS ARE NOW EXIT-CODE GATES. (a.1) The FK: on_delete: :nothing emits no ON DELETE clause at all, so nothing in the DDL text says NO ACTION and nothing distinguishes it from a cascade without asking pg_constraint directly; the test reads c.confdeltype::text from the live catalog and asserts == "a" with an explicit companion refute == "c" so a failure reads against the criterion's own wording. Ground truth observed from a real replay: ["instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey", "a", "<tenant_schema>.process_definitions", "definition_id", "id"]. (a.2) The partial unique index: asserted three ways. Structurally, pg_indexes.indexdef is split on " WHERE " and the predicate asserted to mention status and to contain the literal DERIVED from Ecto.Enum.mappings(ProcessDefinition, :status)[:active] rather than hard-coded -- so a case change on EITHER side (enum or migration) fails. Note Postgres normalises the predicate to `((status)::text = 'active'::text)`, NOT the migration's literal `status = 'active'`, so a naive substring check on the criterion's own SQL fragment would have failed; the test asserts against the extracted predicate instead. Behaviourally, 'a second definition activated ...' inserts two DRAFT rows sharing a name (the discriminator that separates this from a total unique index on name -- without it the suite would pass against the wrong index entirely), reads the stored literal straight out of the column and asserts it is "draft" and equal to its own String.downcase/1, activates the first via the guarded single-statement UPDATE REQ-030 will use, asserts it loads back as the :active atom (closing the dump/load round trip), and asserts the second activation returns {:error, %Postgrex.Error{}} with postgres.code == :unique_violation and postgres.constraint == "uq_active_definition". If the enum dumped a different case the index would match ZERO rows and that second UPDATE would simply SUCCEED -- which is precisely the silent failure now gated. schemas_test carries the pure half: Ecto.Enum.dump_values/2 == ["draft", "active", "deprecated", "archived"] and every dumped value equals its own downcase. (b) THE DOUBLE-WRITTEN graph DEFAULT: 'the DB column default for graph and the schema module's struct default are the same value' inserts a row by raw SQL that omits graph entirely (so the DATABASE default fills the column -- a changeset insert would send the schema module's own literal and could never detect a disagreement), reads it back through ProcessDefinition and asserts it equals %ProcessDefinition{}.graph; it also refutes is_nil(column_default) so 'both sides absent' cannot pass vacuously, and separately asserts the shared value really is %{"nodes" => [], "edges" => []} so both agreeing on a WRONG value still fails. A sibling test does the same for the status default against Ecto.Enum's :draft mapping. (c) SECTION 4 GUARD-TEST CLEANUP EXTENDED: test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs gains a @later_tenant_scoped_tables attribute (["process_definitions", "instance_definition_snapshots"]) appended to the on_exit defensive-cleanup list, so a REQ-027 guard regression cannot strand a stray public.process_definitions in a database shared with a concurrently running worktree. NO ASSERTION IN THAT FILE WAS CHANGED -- the guard test already iterates tenant_scoped_migrations/0, which now returns nine entries including REQ-027's two. That is the only existing test file touched, and only for that purpose. (d) THE MIGRATIONS WERE NOT REFORMATTED -- neither migration file was touched at all; `MIX_ENV=test mix format --check-formatted` exits 0 for the project as shipped (ISS-0016: .formatter.exs excludes priv/repo/migrations/**). (e) on_delete: :nothing WAS NOT FLIPPED TO CASCADE -- no migration or schema module was modified in this step. The delete-rejection test asserts the designed PD-08 behaviour and changes nothing, and the moduledoc assertion pins the sentence 'Adding `on_delete: :delete_all` here would destroy exactly the data this table exists to preserve' so ISS-0024's invitation to 'fix' it stays gated. || REAL TEST OUTPUT. Targeted run: `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/definitions/schemas_test.exs test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs --seed 0` -> 'Running ExUnit with seed: 0, max_cases: 32 / Finished in 7.7 seconds (0.3s async, 7.4s sync) / Result: 36 passed'. Full suite run 1 (seed 459582): 'Finished in 35.9 seconds (1.4s async, 34.5s sync) / Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)'. Full suite run 3 (seed 814905): 'Finished in 30.4 seconds (1.0s async, 29.3s sync) / Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)'. 307 = the 271 baseline + exactly the 36 new tests; nothing regressed. Full suite run 2 (--seed 0) returned 'Result: 306/307 passed (4/4 properties, 302/303 tests) / Failed: 1 test' whose ONLY failure was '1) test method short-circuit -- no DB query at all for a non-write method a GET request issues no Ecto query at all (method short-circuit, no DB round-trip) (Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatusTest) test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:121' -- ISS-0011 exactly, at the exact recorded line, under the exact seed ISS-0011's own UPDATE blocks record as NOT safe. Not mine, not fixed; runs 1 and 3 were clean, per ISS-0011's own guidance to re-run rather than conclude from a single red run. || WORKSPACE HYGIENE VERIFIED AFTER THE RUNS: zero leftover schemas matching tenant\_% or req027%, zero rows in tenants and tenant_schemas, and public contains only [approvals, groups, schema_migrations, tenant_role, tenant_schemas, tenants, transition_events, users] -- no stray process_definitions or instance_definition_snapshots. The only test/DB commands issued in this step ran under MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 (letflow_test2); letflow_test and letflow_dev were never touched, docker compose up was never run, and no branch was changed (verified feature/WF02-REQ027-20260816 via git branch --show-current before any file was touched). || DETERMINISM: no DateTime.utc_now/0 anywhere -- every timestamp is a fixed literal (~U[2026-01-02 03:04:05.000000Z] / ~N[2026-01-02 03:04:05.000000]); uniqueness comes from Ecto.UUID.generate/0 and System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) (a VM counter, not an RNG and not a clock); every DB-touching test gets its own Tenant, its own physical Postgres schema and its own Registration row, so no identifier is shared; no test depends on execution order; no hardcoded secrets or connection strings (the database is reached only through Letflow.Repo, which reads config/test.exs). No property test is owed here -- REQ-027 builds schema only; PD-04's closed transition set is REQ-030's, where test_developer_guide.md section 4's property convention applies.

issues.description: Same defect class as Step 2d carry-forward (c), one requirement earlier and NOT fixed here because it is outside this handoff's stated scope ('add the two new table names'). test/letflow/event_store/migrations_test.exs's section 4 guard test now iterates all NINE registered tenant-scoped migrations, but its on_exit defensive-cleanup list still omits REQ-024's 'event_type_registry'. If REQ-024's guard pattern ever regresses, that test would leave a stray public.event_type_registry behind in a database shared with a concurrently running worktree -- exactly the hazard carry-forward (c) was raised to close for REQ-027's two tables. One-word fix: append "event_type_registry" to @later_tenant_scoped_tables. Flagging rather than doing it, since it belongs to REQ-024 and this step was told the file may be modified only for REQ-027's two names.

Observation for TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and for any future test asserting an index predicate: Postgres does NOT store or report a partial index's WHERE clause as written. pg_indexes.indexdef renders uq_active_definition's predicate as `WHERE ((status)::text = 'active'::text)`, not as the migration's (and REQ-027 acceptance criterion 2's) literal `WHERE status = 'active'`. A test asserting the criterion's SQL fragment verbatim against indexdef would fail against a fully correct schema. test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs handles this by extracting the predicate substring and asserting on its components (mentions `status`, contains the literal Ecto.Enum dumps for :active) rather than on the raw fragment. Recorded so the next author of an index-predicate assertion does not lose time rediscovering it.
